finding.text: No shot of any new variant: shots/ holds only `/framework/ui/card/` (sheet.png, 400/1200/1920/3440), which shows the old top specimen, not `titled`, `stack`, `tree-rows`, `fit`. The brief asked for `?at=ui/card/tree-rows` at 400 and 1200 and `fit` at 3440 (Requirements A, check). Layout, sizing, wrapping and spacing for the new work are unverified.

The two urls from the ArrowDown key test are not in the task folder. The brief (B) asked for them in the log, and `session.jsonl` has no `location.search` pair. No Library test or script was added either, so nothing proves the keys work.

`ui/card/page.js` (the `## Four variants, not six` heading, line ~129) is stale: the page now has nine variants. `ui/card/doc/architecture.md:24` ("Decided: linked, media, action and list…") still names `list`, which was renamed `compact`. The `/framework/ui/card/list/` url now 404s, and old audit data links to it.

`ux/Inbox/readme.md:30-31` still presents `.flush-stack` as the Inbox's own rule. It moved to `framework.css` (`util` layer), so the readme must say where it lives and that `ui/card`'s `stack` also uses it. `styles/` has no index line for the class either.

A fresh agent cannot continue from the task folder alone: there is no outcome and no commit list. `session.jsonl` ends with a harness-completed close ("agent ended its turn without completing"), the smoke run result is absent, and the "ui-kit gap" line found (`/live/demos/page.jsonl` bare-string line) has no follow-up task. The extra loose pngs in shots/ (framework-1920, framework-library-1920, framework-ux-Inbox-1920, framework-ui-card-1920) belong to no named question and are unindexed.

`fit` is `.measure.start` with an inline `--measure: 22em`, and `titled` sets font sizes inline. The brief allowed this only "beyond what the existing variants already do". Both carry notes, so it is acceptable, but it is a second inline-style pattern for the kit.

The `keydown` listener is added once and never removed (`this.listening` guard), and the key map moves the rail with wrap-around. Wrap-around was not in the brief; harmless, but say so in the library readme.
